relationships.subject: ATPA
relationships.evidence_quote: bath perfusion of ATPA (20 min) elicited LTD in ACC brain slices in a dose-dependent manner

relationships.subject: UBP310
relationships.evidence_quote: the GluK1 antagonist UBP310 effectively abolished ATPA-induced LTD

relationships.subject: nimodipine
relationships.evidence_quote: Nimodipine (20 µM), an L-type voltage-gated calcium channel (L-VGCC) blocker, prevented the induction of KA-induced LTD

relationships.subject: KT-5720
relationships.evidence_quote: The PKA inhibitor KT-5720 (2 µM) significantly attenuated KA-induced LTD

relationships.subject: picrotoxin
relationships.evidence_quote: the administration of the non-competitive GABAA receptor antagonist picrotoxin (100 µM) effectively abolished both KA-induced LTD

relationships.subject: spared nerve injury
relationships.evidence_quote: Collectively, these data suggest that peripheral nerve injury induces selective up-regulation of GluK1 and GluK2/3 subunits in the ACC

relationships.subject: spared nerve injury
relationships.evidence_quote: Conversely, LTD induction was markedly occluded in SNI mice

relationships.subject: ATPA
relationships.evidence_quote: bilateral intra-ACC administration of ATPA (1.25 ng) significantly attenuated both mechanical allodynia and thermal hyperalgesia

key_findings: GluK1-containing kainate receptors mediate a novel LTD in the ACC requiring L-type VGCCs, PKA and GABAA receptor activity, but not NMDARs.
KAR-LTD is occluded in SNI mice despite GluK1 upregulation; intra-ACC ATPA is analgesic but not anxiolytic.
